summary: Namco/Bandai Namco's Ace Combat series mixes arcade flight combat with campaign storytelling, with Ace Combat 3 especially split between Japanese and international content scopes.

entries.title: Ace Combat 3
entries.definitive_edition: Japanese PlayStation release for complete content

emulation.emulator: DuckStation/Mednafen only if hardware is unavailable
emulation.notes: Use owned disc image and record emulator/BIOS settings.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Japanese PlayStation release with route/translation state documented

primary.version: Japanese Ace Combat 3: Electrosphere, with translation state documented if used
primary.why: The Japanese two-disc release contains the full branching story, missions, and presentation, while international releases were heavily reduced. For a content-complete archive run, the Japanese PlayStation version is the main route, with fan translation clearly labeled if used.
primary.how_to_play: Use an owned Japanese PlayStation copy on original hardware or accurate PS1 emulation. Record region, disc, translation patch state, route/ending, mission, difficulty, aircraft, memory-card state, and whether the reduced international release was compared.

secondary.why: It lacks much of the Japanese story and branching content.

all_releases.reason: secondary: compare only for localization/content cuts.

all_releases.fidelity: Unofficial translation of the Japanese content.
all_releases.reason: secondary: accessibility route; label clearly as fan translation.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Japanese and international versions differ drastically; translation patches are unofficial.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record region and translation state; do not use the international release as a full substitute.

entries.title: Air Combat
entries.definitive_edition: Original PlayStation Air Combat / Ace Combat release

emulation.notes: Use an owned disc image, conservative internal-resolution scaling, and original 4:3 framing.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: High-resolution PlayStation emulation without widescreen geometry breakage.

primary.version: Original PlayStation Air Combat / Ace Combat release
primary.why: Bandai Namco identifies the PlayStation game as the first Ace Combat title. It is a newly built campaign rather than a port of the separate 1993 arcade game, and the only other same-game release was an obsolete Japanese mobile conversion.
primary.how_to_play: Use an owned PlayStation disc with a current accurate emulator, raise internal resolution conservatively, preserve 4:3, and keep the original frame pacing unless a tested emulator option fixes presentation without changing game speed.

all_releases.fidelity: Original 17-mission console campaign with split-screen multiplayer and unlockables.
all_releases.reason: primary: content authority and only practical complete release.

all_releases.fidelity: Japanese budget reissue of the PlayStation game.
all_releases.reason: primary-equivalent: same game data in a later retail printing.
skip: unavailable legacy mobile route and not a higher-fidelity replacement.

all_releases.fidelity: Separate predecessor on Namco System 21 hardware.
all_releases.reason: skip for this entry: the PlayStation team created a new game instead of porting the arcade version; archive it separately.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The PlayStation release is the complete campaign target. The 1993 arcade Air Combat is a separate predecessor, not exclusive content within this game.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster exists. Do not mistake the separate 1993 arcade Air Combat or 1995 Air Combat 22 for ports of the PlayStation campaign, and do not stretch the 4:3 image.
